title: Colocated cluster seed & rollout automation guide (working notes)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working guide for seeding and rolling out Kubernetes control and worker planes across colocated racks that mix vSphere VMs and bare-metal servers (common customer pattern). The doc focuses on automation patterns (Terraform + PXE/Ignition + Ansible), safety gates for upgrades, and pragmatic rollback strategies.

Status and intent:
- Draft, operational notes: intended for infra engs who will run field deployments or vendor partners.
- Not a final runbook: contains TODOs, questions for solutions engineering, and pointers to implementation PRs.

High-level approach summary:
1) Immutable OS images (signed) for both VM and baremetal nodes. Use the same Ignition payload + kubeadm bootstrap tokens to ensure identical kubelet config across runtimes.
2) Seed pattern: a small set of resilient seed-nodes (mix: 1-2 vSphere control-plane VMs + 1 baremetal control-plane) to accelerate bootstrap and provide different hardware coverage.
3) Terraform for inventory and secret provisioning: separate modules for vSphere vs BMC/IPMI networks but a shared "node-object" abstraction (metadata + tags).
4) PXE/ISO fallback: baremetal boots via PXE to installer image; vSphere uses ovf template with ignition attached. Both converge to the same OS image with the same unit file to join cluster.
5) Upgrade/rollout uses time-based canaries with health gates + automatic evict/fallback when thresholds exceed error budgets.

Detailed components and notes:
A) Terraform modules (notes & pitfalls)
- modules/bmc: manages catalog of IPMI/BMC endpoints, VLAN assignment, power-cycle credentials. Make sure to store BMC creds in KMS (do not in TF state).
- modules/vsphere: resource pool reservation, folder placement, tag set (rack, rack-uplink, power-pair). Avoid implicit datacenter assumptions; modules accept datacenter_id inputs.
- modules/node-meta: small wrapper that normalizes labels/taints/hostnames across providers (tag mapping). This is what higher-level bootstrap tasks reference.
- Known issues: vSphere templates need identical NIC ordering to match ignition network config; call out nic index mapping in module outputs.

B) Bootstrapping sequence (operator checklist)
Preparation (preflight)
- Validate hardware manifests: rack map, BMC IPs, NIC mappings, racked-uplink per node.
- Ensure KMS entries for all BMC and ovf passwords: run kms-tool verify.
- Confirm PXE DHCP scopes for the rack: netmask, router, next-server.
- vSphere: ensure datastore has space for templates and that resource pools are unsaturated.

Seed bootstrap steps (ordered):
1. Provision node metadata via Terraform (node-meta + bmc/vsphere modules) -> outputs provide power IPs, hostnames.
2. Push signed OS image to image-server and publish Ignition blobs keyed by cluster-id + role.
3. Kick off PXE for baremetal seed-1 and deploy ovf for vSphere seed-1. Power-cycle via BMC.
4. Watch ros-console for first-boot logs. Confirm kubelet registration flags and kubeadm init success on first control-plane seed.
5. Join additional seed control-plane nodes one-by-one, verify etcd quorum after each join.
6. Promote seed nodes to control-plane and annotate in node-meta.
7. Gradually add worker nodes (vSphere then baremetal or interleaved based on capacity plan).

C) Canary/upgrade plan (control-plane and worker upgrades)
Principles:
- Minimize in-place changes: prefer replace-by-image for nodes (immutable).
- Strict health gates: pod restart rate, API latency, etcd commit latency.
- Canary window: 30m default for critical upgrades; scale based on cluster size.

Automation sequence for a minor kubelet/kubeadm control-plane upgrade:
1. Snapshot etcd and archive to s3-compatible location (automated via cronjob).
2. Select a canary host in each hardware class (one vSphere control-plane VM, one baremetal control-plane) and drain with PodDisruptionBudget awareness.
3. Destroy and reprovision canary with new image (using TF to mark desired image tag).
4. Run smoke tests: api-server health, a small synthetic trace (latency < 150ms), etcd commit latency < 30ms, core DNS queries 200ms, replica count 100% after 5m.
5. If smoke passes, expand canary to 10% of control-plane nodes (maintain quorum) then to 25% and finally to 100% with configurable pauses.
6. Roll worker groups by rack/region: prefer not to update >25% of workers in a rack at once.
7. If any step exceeds thresholds, auto-rollback: reprovision previous signed image and rejoin.

D) Safety checks and post-upgrade validation
- Metrics to capture before/during/after: api-server quantiles, etcd leader changes, kube-scheduler latency, node rejoin times, average pod restart rate per minute.
- Tracing hooks: attach a short-lived sidecar that emits synthetic traces for the default ingress and a health-check deployment.
- Alerting rules: set short-duration alerts for gateway errors and CPU saturation during canary windows and suppress non-actionable alerts via temporary silence during rollouts.

E) Rollback strategy
- Fast rollback for node image: reapply previous signed image tag and reprovision the node. This assumes state is preserved externally (PV behaviour considered separately).
- Cluster-level rollback (rare): if control-plane regression is severe across multiple canaries, revert CNI + control-plane images as a coordinated operation. Document contact list and execute incident postmortem.

F) Observability + traceability
- Keep a cluster bootstrap record (small JSON) per deployment in S3 with: terraform commit sha, ignition blob id, os-image tag, seed nodes list, initial etcd snapshot id. Use this for reproducing or debugging field failures.
- Stream first-boot systemd logs to central log collector (filebeat/rsyslog) with tags: cluster-id, rack, node-slot.

G) Field runbook (short checklist for on-site tech)
- Step 0: Confirm power and network patching per rack document.
- Step 1: Confirm BMC login and power-cycle ability (test using bmc-tool power status).
- Step 2: Trigger PXE/OVF as instructed in TF outputs.
- Step 3: Watch console, copy bootstrap token to SRE slack channel.
- Step 4: If node fails to join within 12 minutes: grab system journal, call the infra rotation pager.

H) Terraform/operational gotchas and tips
- Avoid storing BMC passwords in state: use vault or KMS and reference with data sources.
- Use a tag/label policy that supports selective rollouts (e.g., hardware_class: h1, rack: r12, env: prod).
- Ship a staged ovf template for vSphere with included guestinfo that points to ignition URL instead of baking ignition into template. This allows single template for multiple clusters.

I) Security and compliance notes
- All ignition blobs must be signed and have a TTL. In the field we saw mis-boot due to stale ignition blobs; TTL prevents reconciling to out-of-date configs.
- KMS access should be audited per deployment and short-lived service principals used for initial provisioning.

Open questions / TODOs:
- TODO: define canonical PV migration approach when reprovisioning worker nodes (CSI specifics per customer).
- Question: should we integrate Cluster API (CAPI) for lifecycle vs current ad-hoc TF+scripts approach? Tradeoffs: CAPI offers declarative machine management but adds complexity and operator burden.
- TODO: automate preflight NIC-index mapping detection by scanning firmware/udev on a live node image.
- TODO: add a failure-mode matrix for control-plane tandem failures (power loss vs kernel panic vs network partition) and test playbooks.

References and quick links:
- GH PR: terraform-modules/pull/218 (node-meta refactor)
- Confluence: Onprem-Deployment-Blueprint (design overview)
- Jira: PD-4823 (colocated rack pilot)
- Slack: #private-deployments (seed pattern discussion)

Notes to self / rough timeline for next iteration:
- Iterate TF modules to produce a single node manifest (metadata + desired-image) and add a small controller that reconciles ignition blobs off of that manifest. 2-week spike.
- Run a staged lab deployment (1 rack) with synthetic load and run upgrade plan to validate health gates. 1-week runbook test.

End.
